mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, market participants anticipate prolonged high policy rates, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to deliver a statistically significant negative alpha at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode corporate profit margins and consumer spending power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods, or the mechanism produces a positive rank IC.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for two consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces output, ultimately depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative alpha is not robust to a 5% significance threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases real discount rates and inflation risk premia, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to produce negative 20-day returns in at least 55% of triggered instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-on-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the prior six-month average, combined with a concurrent rise in personal savings (RSAFS), signals a housing demand recovery that boosts construction and related equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the interaction rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the prior 12-month average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 fails to deliver positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the positive alpha is not significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates reduced household buffer capacity, which increases sensitivity to income shocks and can depress consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 65% of triggered episodes, or the negative alpha is not robust across two economic cycles.
